definition: A quantity with both a magnitude (size) and a direction, such as a displacement, velocity or force, printed in bold as $\boldsymbol{v}$ or written $\overrightarrow{AB}$, unlike a scalar, which has a magnitude only.

A vector of magnitude 1; the unit vector in the direction of a non-zero vector $\boldsymbol{v}$ is $\frac{\boldsymbol{v}}{\lvert\boldsymbol{v}\rvert}$, found by dividing every component by $\lvert\boldsymbol{v}\rvert$ (normalising).

The unit vectors $\boldsymbol{i}$, $\boldsymbol{j}$ and $\boldsymbol{k}$, one unit along the positive $x$-, $y$- and $z$-axes, so that any vector can be written $v_{1}\boldsymbol{i} + v_{2}\boldsymbol{j} + v_{3}\boldsymbol{k}$.

One of the numbers $v_{1}$, $v_{2}$, $v_{3}$ in $\boldsymbol{v} = v_{1}\boldsymbol{i} + v_{2}\boldsymbol{j} + v_{3}\boldsymbol{k}$, giving how far the vector goes along the $x$-, $y$- or $z$-axis, written in that order in a column vector.

The length of a vector, $\lvert\boldsymbol{v}\rvert = \sqrt{v_{1}^{2} + v_{2}^{2} + v_{3}^{2}}$ for $\boldsymbol{v} = v_{1}\boldsymbol{i} + v_{2}\boldsymbol{j} + v_{3}\boldsymbol{k}$, which is a scalar and never negative.
The arrow from a fixed origin O to a point A, labelled $\overrightarrow{OA}$ or $\boldsymbol{a}$; its components equal the coordinates of A.
The rate of change of position, a vector that gives both how fast and in which direction an object moves; its magnitude is the speed, and in one dimension its sign gives the direction.
How fast an object moves, whatever its direction: the magnitude $\lvert\boldsymbol{v}\rvert$ of its velocity, a scalar that is never negative.
